title: Blackstone's Chant Says Structured Deals Are Fit for Insurance Money
summary: Victoria Chant, senior managing director and global head of capital markets and bank relations at Blackstone Credit and Insurance, says structured deals in private investment-grade can help quality-conscious insurers and pension funds increase returns. She speaks at Bloomberg’s Global Credit Forum. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Stocks Fall as Nvidia’s Earnings Rally Sputters
summary:
Wall Street saw renewed volatility as Nvidia Corp.’s post-earnings rally fizzled out, a sign that investors are looking for more evidence about the durability of the artificial-intelligence trade.
John Mowrey, CIO at NFJ Investment Group, brings us into the market open and talks about what Nvidia and Anthropic mean for the AI trade and value investing. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: New York MTA’s Budget Risks $1 Billion Shortfall in 2030
summary: New York City’s transit system is projecting a nearly $1 billion budget gap in 2030 as increasing healthcare and fuel costs outpace its revenue growth.

title: Tech Stocks Decline as Worries Remain For Nvidia After Earnings
summary: US technology stocks erased gains in the wake of Nvidia Corp.’s earnings, while traders looked to the mammoth market debut of Anthropic PBC as the next key test for the artificial intelligence trade.

title: Newsmax Sues to Block Fox From Integrating With Roku
summary: Conservative news channel Newsmax Inc. sued Fox Corp. Wednesday seeking to block the company’s integration of its $22 billion merger with Roku Inc.

title: Bitcoin Erases Bessent Rally as Leverage and Liquidity Fade
summary: Bitcoin has erased all the gains from its late-summer rally as fading risk appetite and the record hack at exchange Binance drove investors to retreat, leaving the largest token trading in a thinner market increasingly vulnerable to sharp price swings.

title: Interest-Rates are 'Normal for Longer,' Not Higher, Says Ed Yardeni
summary:
Fed officials left rates steady last month after raising their benchmark rate in September for the first time in three years.
Since the last meeting, officials have signaled broad agreement over additional hikes, but offered differing views on the appropriate pace.
Ed Yardeni, Founder of Yardeni Research, discusses the markets and his interest-rate outlook. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Warsh Is Closer to Waller on Fed Policy, Gopinath Says
summary: Gita Gopinath, former IMF deputy managing director, says Fed Chair Kevin Warsh has to "walk the talk" when it comes to bringing inflation down to its target of 2%. She says Warsh is closer to Fed Governor Christopher Waller on monetary policy. Waller is calling for a half-point hike in December.  (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Chicago’s Third CFO This Year Saw Budget Red Flags Before Exit
summary: The sudden departure of Chicago’s third chief financial officer in a year came after she repeatedly raised concerns about budgeting practices, including inconsistent deficit calculations.

title: SQM Is Expanding Into a Lithium Glut on Price-Recovery Bet
summary: Major lithium supplier SQM is forging ahead with production and investment plans, even as the global market is set to swing back into a surplus, betting robust demand will spur a recovery in prices.

title: Credit Chiefs Warn of ‘Fear Factor’ as Debt Reprices All at Once
summary: A sharp repricing across fixed-income markets in recent months is likely to continue as interest rates remain elevated, causing a shakeout among weaker borrowers across industries.

title: Nike Moves on Investor Day; Lowe's Reports Earnings | Stock Movers
summary:
On this episode of Stock Movers:

- Lowe's (LOW) is also reporting its earnings this morning, a day after competitor Home Depot reported. Bloomberg Intelligence cites steady demand and data from Placer.ai which points to foot-traffic trends similar to the second quarter.
- Nike (NKE) shares are moving following its investor day. The company is projecting a return to market-level expansion in the fiscal year through May 2029, but challenges in its Jordan and Converse brands, as well as its sportswear business, don't have an immediate fix.
- Take-Two Interactive (TTWO) shares are jumping in premarket as its major video game Grand Theft Auto VI is an open-world game set in Vice City, a fictionalized version of Miami, with lifelike graphical fidelity. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Turkey Slaps Main Erdogan Rival Imamoglu With Political Ban
summary: A Turkish court ordered a political ban for Istanbul Mayor Ekrem Imamoglu, President Recep Tayyip Erdogan’s main opponent, paving the way for the ruling party to potentially take control of Turkey’s largest city.

title: Latest Oil Market News and Analysis for Nov. 18
summary: Oil inched lower despite bullish headlines from the Middle East as risk appetite waned in a choppy session.

title: Gold Slumps Below $3,800 as Fed Officials Signal More Rate Hikes
summary: Gold dropped below $3,800 an ounce for the first time since September 2025 after Federal Reserve officials made the case for more interest-rate hikes to tackle stubborn inflation.

title: Was Jensen Huang’s Exit Premature?
summary: Did Nvidia’s board move too soon in ruling out Jensen Huang’s return? New Street Tech Infrastructure Analyst Antoine Chkaiban joined Bloomberg Open Interest to argue that the decision could hurt shareholders, employees, and Nvidia’s long-term edge. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Adler’s Ex-Legal Chief Settles Criminal Case Amid Ongoing Probe
summary: The former legal chief at Adler Group SA has agreed to pay an undisclosed amount to settle a criminal investigation against him as he cooperates with a wider probe into the real estate firm over long-running allegations made by a whistleblower and short-sellers.

title: Treasuries Higher for a Third Day as Risk Appetite Ebbs
summary: Benchmark US Treasuries rose for a third day with support from setbacks for US stocks, falling oil prices and speculation that most of the Federal Reserve’s upcoming interest-rate hikes are already priced in.

title: Copper Plunges Over 5% as AI Trade Unravels in Metals Markets
summary: Copper plunged in a broad selloff across London, New York and Shanghai, as bullish investors bailed on bets tied to the AI boom and others turned outright bearish even as extreme squeezes roil metals markets.
